title: One Balance Behind Every Card Issued on a Mountain Dining Plans Plan
content:
A plan in the Mountain Dining Plans range holds one balance and issues the cards the plan includes against it, so a household with four cards draws on one pot rather than four. Cards beyond those the plan includes are issued against the plan's extra card fee.

A dependant may hold a card only up to the number of dependants the plan allows and only where they meet the plan's minimum holder age; alcohol is never paid for on a dependant's card whatever the plan allows the named holder.

The daily and per-transaction caps stand against the plan as a whole and not against each card, so two cards spending together on one day are measured together against the daily cap.

A corporate account takes only the plans this charter sells to corporate accounts, and on those plans the cards are issued to named employees exactly as they are to the named dependants of a household.

## The one pot, put as a condition and its result

| What the household presents | What is measured | What comes off |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Any card issued on the plan | the plan's one balance | that balance, and no other |
| Two cards spending on the same day | the day's spending on the plan as a whole against the plan's daily limit | that one balance |
| A single transaction on any one card | that transaction against the plan's per-transaction limit | that one balance |

## A day measured across two cards

Take hypothetical figures on one plan: one card is presented in the morning for $120.00 and a second card is presented that afternoon for $95.00. The two are measured together, so $215.00 has been spent on the plan that day and it is that total, not either transaction on its own, that is set against the plan's daily limit. The plan's per-transaction limit meanwhile answers each of the two transactions separately.

## A dependant's card

A dependant's card is issued only where the plan allows a dependant at all, only up to the number of dependants the plan allows, and only where the dependant meets the plan's minimum holder age. On a plan that admits alcohol, the admission runs to the named holder and not to the dependant: alcohol is never paid for on a dependant's card. On a corporate account, a card issued to a named employee stands exactly as a card issued to a named dependant of a household stands.
